Principle 07 of 8

Accountability

Explain decisions, offer recourse, own mistakes, and protect people who speak up.

Protects

Everyone affected by a decision

Why it matters

Power without a way to question it is easy to abuse. People need to know why something happened and what they can do about it.

Covers

Disclosure and decision opacity (5.2, 5.4), governance failures (6.6), breach notification (4.12), and governance, whistleblowing, and corporate accountability (Category 15).

1.8 Billing Errors & Unauthorized Charges · 7 practices

Accountability+ Honesty
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
1.8.1Bill CrammingAdding unauthorized charges — third-party services, premium SMS, mystery fees — to invoices without explicit consent.Telecom, utilities, hospitality
1.8.2Estimated-Billing OverchargeSystematically estimating bills on the high side rather than from actual meter or usage data, requiring customers to identify and dispute.Energy utilities, water utilities
1.8.3Damage-Claim FabricationCharging customers for pre-existing damage, normal wear, or fabricated incidents after departure without dispute opportunity.Hospitality, automotive (lease return), real estate (security deposits)
1.8.4Inactivity / Maintenance DrainCharging maintenance or inactivity fees that slowly drain dormant accounts to zero.Financial services, gift cards, fashion (gift balances)
1.8.5Zombie Subscription ChargingContinuing to bill after cancellation or account deletion by retaining payment tokens and citing "billing-cycle completion."Fitness, dating, cleaning services, cosmetics, financial services
1.8.6Coordination-of-Benefits FraudBilling multiple insurers for the full allowed amount rather than coordinating, resulting in overpayment or balance billing.Dental, healthcare
1.8.7Insurance Code UpcodingCoding procedures at higher reimbursement levels than clinically warranted to inflate insurance billing.Healthcare, dental
